resources.string: Also the birthdays and death anniversaries of those no longer with us.
Android was asked and said no, so reminders stay off.
Notifications for f-tree are turned off in Android\'s settings, so no reminder can be shown.
A note on the morning of a birthday, if you turn reminders on in f-tree\'s settings.

Most people should leave this off. Betas are unfinished builds put out to be tested — they can be slow, wrong, or lose work, and a fix may take days. You will be offered them ahead of everyone else, which is the point and also the risk.
Turn on “Check for updates” above first. This only changes which release the updater offers you; on its own it does nothing.

A beta is a version that has not been through a full release. It may misbehave in ways the stable app does not, and turning this off afterwards will not move you back — Android will not install an older version over a newer one, so you will stay on betas until the next stable release passes the one you are on.
Export your tree before you install one.

Six that never ask, and two that do. Two are for the updater: internet access to ask GitHub about releases, and permission to install an update. Three are for nearby sharing: to see the Wi-Fi network, to hear other devices on it, and to check a connection exists. One is for birthday reminders: to set the morning\'s reminder again after the phone restarts. The two that ask are the camera, only if you choose to scan a code, and you can always type instead; and notifications, only when you turn birthday reminders on. Nothing leaves the device except when you deliberately send it, to a device you can see, on a network you are already on, with no account and nothing in between.

Off unless you turn it on. Sends your tree straight to a phone or computer on the same Wi-Fi — no account, nothing in between — and only after the other device says yes. Nothing can see this device until you open one of the screens below.
Pick a device on this Wi-Fi and check the same six digits appear on both screens.
What arrives goes through the same review as an imported file. Nothing is added until you confirm.
Seen by other devices on the Wi-Fi while a nearby screen is open. The name is made up on purpose, so it doesn\'t announce yours.

The code changes once it has been used, and every five minutes. Scanning it skips the six digits, because only a device that can see this screen can read it.

Android is set to refuse f-tree the camera. You can change that in the app\'s settings, or pick the device from the list or type its address instead.
